=== PUBLIC TURN 2/2 ===
## NO_GO — not ready for implementation

The gate is based on authoritative policy and reproducible evidence, not reviewer count.

- `DELETE /ledger/{entry_id}` contradicts the append-only ledger policy. Corrections must use compensating entries. `[AIP-01]`
- A `support_agent` can post a refund, reproduced three of three times, directly violating the authorization policy. `[AIP-02]`
- `POST /refunds` lacks server-side role enforcement and trusts caller-supplied `actor_id`; actor identity must come from authenticated server context. `[AIP-03]`
- The financial posting contract lacks idempotency and deterministic replay behavior, creating duplicate-posting risk. `[AIP-04]`
- “Internal network” and “permission can be added later” are rejected as readiness arguments because they do not resolve the policy conflict or demonstrated bypass. `[AIP-05]`

Required before a fresh verification round:

1. Remove ledger deletion and define append-only compensating corrections.
2. Enforce `finance_approver` server-side; verify `support_agent` is denied without ledger mutation.
3. Derive actor identity from authentication, not request data.
4. Define atomic idempotency semantics and test sequential/concurrent replay and post-commit timeout cases.

Public evidence ledger:

| ID | Disposition | Source role | Evidence locator |
|---|---|---|---|
| AIP-01 | Accepted blocker | `role-ledger-integrity-r1` | Confirmed append-only policy; draft `DELETE /ledger/{entry_id}` |
| AIP-02 | Accepted blocker | `role-authorization-integrity-r1` | Role policy; `support_token_posts_refund`, reproduced 3/3 |
| AIP-03 | Accepted blocker | `role-authorization-integrity-r1` | Draft `POST /refunds`: caller `actor_id`, no server role checks |
| AIP-04 | Accepted blocker | `role-refund-contract-reliability-r1` | Draft lacks idempotency; runtime confirms durable ledger side effect |
| AIP-05 | Rejected proposal | `role-authorization-integrity-r1` | Prior internal-network comments versus policy and runtime evidence |

All three planned roles completed without degradation or missing coverage: ledger and authorization in wave 1; API reliability in wave 2. Business refund limits remained out of scope.
